stories.title: Russian cruise missile breaches Polish airspace during Western military exercise
stories.summary: Early Friday, three objects entered Poland’s airspace, one of which was identified as a Russian cruise missile, according to Polish authorities. No injuries or damage were reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the intrusion did not appear accidental and described it as a provocation from Moscow, occurring while Western allies were conducting a large‑scale military exercise in the region.
stories.why: The incident heightens concerns that the Ukraine conflict could spill into NATO territory, prompting increased security alerts.

stories.title: RBI likely to raise repo rate to 5.75% in December, 6% by February, poll shows
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to increase its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December, according to a Reuters poll reported by the Economic Times. A further 25‑basis‑point hike is projected for February, taking the rate to 6% as inflation is seen breaching the RBI’s 6% tolerance limit, with rising energy costs and uneven monsoon rainfall identified as contributing factors.

stories.title: Anthropic shares drop up to 7.4% in pre‑market trade on day two
stories.summary: Anthropic’s stock fell as much as 7.4% in pre‑market trading on its second day of trading, reversing part of the 39% jump it posted after its record‑setting IPO. The decline occurred amid a broad market sell‑off and investor worries about a steep valuation and competitive pressures in the AI sector. Despite the dip, the shares closed the day 17% above the IPO price.
stories.why: The move signals early investor caution toward the AI firm’s high valuation and may influence sentiment toward similar tech IPOs.

stories.title: Europe says it is ready to negotiate with Russia to end Ukraine war
stories.summary: At a Berlin summit of the “Coalition of the Willing,” European leaders said they have a united negotiating position and are prepared to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Europe is clear and consistent, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called Moscow’s maximalist demands unrealistic. US envoy Jared Kushner said President Trump wants a deal with Moscow alongside Europe, and President Vladimir Putin has rejected any European role in the US‑led peace talks.
stories.why: A coordinated European stance could shape diplomatic dynamics and affect the chances of a peace settlement.

stories.title: Rupee appreciation could cut earnings for Indian IT firms, report says
stories.summary: A new report says the strengthening Indian rupee may lower earnings for Indian IT companies. The stronger rupee against foreign currencies is expected to hit profitability, particularly for firms with significant exposure to European markets. With traditional cost‑saving measures becoming scarce, maintaining margins will be challenging amid the current economic environment.
